source.title: Stable Minima of ReLU Neural Networks Suffer from the Curse of Dimensionality: The Neural Shattering Phenomenon
source.authors: Tong-Tong Liang; Dan Qiao; Yu-Xiang Wang; Rahul Parhi

record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-descent training outcomes in synthetic regression, a new setting relative to the classification-focused versions; none of the listed versions is directly tested.
record.gate_note: The paper reports synthetic regression training MSE and neuron activation results. These bear on training outcomes but do not measure classification error or the specific mechanisms and benchmark settings named in V1–V6. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4 and Figure 3 report the V5 edge-of-stability behavior in a new synthetic regression setting: full-batch GD sharpness oscillates around 2/η while training loss decreases. The record misses this result and incorrectly treats every version as untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion. More precisely, under the paper's two-layer ReLU and uniform-ball assumptions, stable solutions have vanishing generalization gaps and estimation-error bounds whose sample complexity suffers the curse of dimensionality. Boundary-localized, sparsely activating neurons explain this weakness, and simulations corroborate it. The reported clean-target MSE values must not be interpreted as noisy-label training loss.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use two-layer regression networks on synthetic noisy data, not gradient-based classification on CIFAR benchmarks; the paper studies stable minima and weight decay rather than the listed classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Input dimension, learning rate, and weight decay change reported training outcomes; the paper reports lower training MSE with weight decay in its comparison and dimension-dependent outcomes in its experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports clean-target MSE 1.1048 without weight decay at η=0.9 versus 0.0550 with λ=0.1 at η=0.01; noisy-label training losses are 0.1796 and 1.1135, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this synthetic regression comparison, the large-step unregularized run fits noisy labels more closely but estimates the clean target less accurately than the smaller-step weight-decay run.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 clean-target MSE values for d=1 through 6 are 0.3412, 0.0275, 0.0711, 0.1253, 0.1978, and 0.2453. Noisy-label training loss decreases across these dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this dimension sweep, fitting noisy labels improves with dimension while clean-target estimation deteriorates from d=2 through 6; d=1 is an exception to a monotonic estimation-error trend.

record.problems: The empirical experiments concern synthetic regression with two-layer networks, not the classification benchmarks or architectures in the versions. The reported numerical experiment summaries do not provide error bars for the cited terminal MSE values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure-only sweep values and other plotted metrics are not separately extracted because the text already provides representative explicit numerical results and the remaining plotted conditions are not needed to establish any tested version.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and the stated recipe comparisons.

Spurious-local-minimum frequencies in realizable ReLU teacher-student problems as teacher/student widths grow, and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons. V2 concerns regression optimization, not classification specifically.
Depth degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth; Kaiming initialization is used without comparison.

Initial linearized-model stability thresholds; above-threshold catapult recovery and curvature reduction; divergence at larger rates or from initially subthreshold runs. The reported threshold oscillations do not establish these additional behaviors or a rise toward the threshold from below.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Add linked V5 rows for Figure 3's η=0.9 no-decay run: the largest Hessian eigenvalue oscillates around 2/η≈2.2 while noisy-label training loss decreases over 50,000 epochs to 0.1796. Record the early gradient clipping. These optimization dynamics are distinct from the omitted generalization sweeps and are necessary to assess V5.
missing.locator: Section 4, Neural shattering; Figure 3, top-middle training curves and top-right Hessian curve; Section 4 footnote 7

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. The stability equivalence in Proposition 2.1 is attributed to prior work; the verdict instead rests on the study's own measured dynamics in Figure 3. None of R1–R8 directly measures a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student classification of local minima across teacher/student widths.
Depth comparisons for plain versus residual networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10, and the stated special-initialization or normalization conditions.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth, including very deep tanh or convolutional networks.
Recovery above a stability threshold, curvature behavior at that threshold, and divergence conditions.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup residual-network comparisons.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network of width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with large step size and no weight decay; authors report the terminal training MSE.

conditions.value: 512 noisy samples of a 10-dimensional linear target; σ = 1

rows.note: The authors say this matches the noise level and describe the network as overfitting.
rows.check: The value 1.1048 measures error against the clean target at training inputs, not loss against noisy training labels. Figure 3 separately reports noisy-label training loss 0.1796. Include gradient clipping at threshold 50 during the first 10 epochs. Clean-target MSE alone does not measure V5.

rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with weight decay; authors report the terminal training MSE.

conditions.value: 512 noisy samples of a 10-dimensional linear target; σ = 1

rows.note: The authors say this model avoids overfitting.
rows.check: The value 0.0550 measures error against the clean target at training inputs, not noisy-label training loss, which Figure 3 reports as 1.1135. The comparison changes both learning rate and weight decay, so it cannot isolate either intervention.

relationships.condition: Width-2048 two-layer ReLU regression network, 512 noisy samples, d=10, full-batch GD with η=0.9 and no weight decay; gradient clipping occurs only during the first 10 epochs.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4 and Figure 3, rather than an existing row: sharpness oscillates around 2/η≈2.2 while noisy-label training loss decreases over the 50,000-epoch run, ending at 0.1796.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness oscillated around 2/η ≈ 2.2 as noisy-label training loss decreased over 50,000 epochs, ending at 0.1796.
